14.L148:
<n>148:1</n> Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
<n>148:2</n> Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli ejus: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes ejus.
<n>148:3</n> Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
<n>148:4</n> Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
<n>148:5</n> Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
<n>148:6</n> Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
<n>148:7</n> Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
<n>148:8</n> Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum ejus:
<n>148:9</n> Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
<n>148:10</n> Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
<n>148:11</n> Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes júdices terræ.
<n>148:12</n> Júvenes, et vírgines: † senes cum junióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * (13) quia exaltátum est nomen ejus solíus.
14.L149:
<n>149:1</n> Cantáte Dómino cánticum novum: * laus ejus in ecclésia sanctórum.
<n>149:2</n> Lætétur Israël in eo, qui fecit eum: * et fílii Sion exsúltent in rege suo.
<n>149:3</n> Laudent nomen ejus in choro: * in týmpano, et psaltério psallant ei:
<n>149:4</n> Quia beneplácitum est Dómino in pópulo suo: * et exaltábit mansuétos in salútem.
<n>149:5</n> Exsultábunt sancti in glória: * lætabúntur in cubílibus suis.
<n>149:6</n> Exaltatiónes Dei in gútture eórum: * et gládii ancípites in mánibus eórum.
<n>149:7</n> Ad faciéndam vindíctam in natiónibus: * increpatiónes in pópulis.
<n>149:8</n> Ad alligándos reges eórum in compédibus: * et nóbiles eórum in mánicis férreis.
<n>149:9</n> Ut fáciant in eis judícium conscríptum: * glória hæc est ómnibus sanctis ejus.
14.E148:
<n>148:1</n> Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.
<n>148:2</n> Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.
<n>148:3</n> Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.
<n>148:4</n> Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.
<n>148:5</n> For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.
<n>148:6</n> He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.
<n>148:7</n> Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:
<n>148:8</n> Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:
<n>148:9</n> Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:
<n>148:10</n> Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:
<n>148:11</n> Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:
<n>148:12</n> Young men and maidens: † let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * (13) For his name alone is exalted.
14.E149:
<n>149:1</n> Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle: * let his praise be in the church of the saints.
<n>149:2</n> Let Israel rejoice in him that made him: * and let the children of Sion be joyful in their king.
<n>149:3</n> Let them praise his name in choir: * let them sing to him with the timbrel and the psaltery.
<n>149:4</n> For the Lord is well pleased with his people: * and he will exalt the meek unto salvation.
<n>149:5</n> The saints shall rejoice in glory: * they shall be joyful in their beds.
<n>149:6</n> The high praises of God shall be in their mouth: * and two-edged swords in their hands:
<n>149:7</n> To execute vengeance upon the nations, * chastisements among the people:
<n>149:8</n> To bind their kings with fetters, * and their nobles with manacles of iron.
<n>149:9</n> To execute upon them the judgment that is written: * this glory is to all his saints.
14.L142:
<n>142:1</n> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam: áuribus pércipe obsecratiónem meam in veritáte tua: * exáudi me in tua justítia.
<n>142:2</n> Et non intres in judícium cum servo tuo: * quia non justificábitur in conspéctu tuo omnis vivens.
<n>142:5</n> Memor fui diérum antiquórum, meditátus sum in ómnibus opéribus tuis: * in factis mánuum tuárum meditábar.
<n>142:6</n> Expándi manus meas ad te: * ánima mea sicut terra sine aqua tibi.
<n>142:9</n> Éripe me de inimícis meis, Dómine, ad te confúgi: * (10a) doce me fácere voluntátem tuam, quia Deus meus es tu.
14.E142:
<n>142:1</n> Hear, O Lord, my prayer: give ear to my supplication in thy truth: * hear me in thy justice.
<n>142:2</n> And enter not into judgment with thy servant: * for in thy sight no man living shall be justified.
<n>142:5</n> I remembered the days of old, I meditated on all thy works: * I meditated upon the works of thy hands.
<n>142:6</n> I stretched forth my hands to thee: * my soul is as earth without water unto thee.
<n>142:9</n> Deliver me from my enemies, O Lord, to thee have I fled: * (10a) teach me to do thy will, for thou art my God.
14.L140:
<n>140:1</n> Dómine, clamávi ad te, exáudi me: * inténde voci meæ, cum clamávero ad te.
<n>140:2</n> Dirigátur orátio mea sicut incénsum in conspéctu tuo: * elevátio mánuum meárum sacrifícium vespertínum.
<n>140:3</n> Pone, Dómine, custódiam ori meo: * et óstium circumstántiæ lábiis meis.
<n>140:4</n> Non declínes cor meum in verba malítiæ, * ad excusándas excusatiónes in peccátis.
<n>140:4</n> Cum homínibus operántibus iniquitátem: * et non communicábo cum eléctis eórum.
<n>140:5</n> Corrípiet me justus in misericórdia, et increpábit me: * óleum autem peccatóris non impínguet caput meum.
<n>140:6</n> Quóniam adhuc et orátio mea in beneplácitis eórum: * absórpti sunt juncti petræ júdices eórum.
<n>140:7</n> Áudient verba mea quóniam potuérunt: * sicut crassitúdo terræ erúpta est super terram.
<n>140:8</n> Dissipáta sunt ossa nostra secus inférnum: * quia ad te, Dómine, Dómine, óculi mei: in te sperávi, non áuferas ánimam meam.
<n>140:9</n> Custódi me a láqueo, quem statuérunt mihi: * et a scándalis operántium iniquitátem.
<n>140:10</n> Cadent in retiáculo ejus peccatóres: * singuláriter sum ego donec tránseam.
14.L141:
<n>141:2</n> Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * voce mea ad Dóminum deprecátus sum:
<n>141:3</n> Effúndo in conspéctu ejus oratiónem meam, * et tribulatiónem meam ante ipsum pronúntio.
<n>141:4</n> In deficiéndo ex me spíritum meum, * et tu cognovísti sémitas meas.
<n>141:4</n> In via hac, qua ambulábam, * abscondérunt láqueum mihi.
<n>141:5</n> Considerábam ad déxteram, et vidébam: * et non erat qui cognósceret me.
<n>141:5</n> Périit fuga a me, * et non est qui requírat ánimam meam.
<n>141:6</n> Clamávi ad te, Dómine, * dixi: Tu es spes mea, pórtio mea in terra vivéntium.
<n>141:7</n> Inténde ad deprecatiónem meam: * quia humiliátus sum nimis.
<n>141:7</n> Líbera me a persequéntibus me: * quia confortáti sunt super me.
<n>141:8</n> Educ de custódia ánimam meam ad confiténdum nómini tuo: * me exspéctant justi, donec retríbuas mihi.
14.E140:
<n>140:1</n> I have cried to thee, O Lord, hear me: * hearken to my voice, when I cry to thee.
<n>140:2</n> Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight; * the lifting up of my hands, as evening sacrifice.
<n>140:3</n> Set a watch, O Lord, before my mouth: * and a door round about my lips.
<n>140:4</n> Incline not my heart to evil words; * to make excuses in sins.
<n>140:4</n> With men that work iniquity: * and I will not communicate with the choicest of them.
<n>140:5</n> The just man shall correct me in mercy, and shall reprove me: * but let not the oil of the sinner fatten my head.
<n>140:6</n> For my prayer also shall still be against the things with which they are well pleased: * their judges falling upon the rock have been swallowed up.
<n>140:7</n> They shall hear my words, for they have prevailed: * as when the thickness of the earth is broken up upon the ground.
<n>140:8</n> Our bones are scattered by the side of hell. * But to thee, O Lord, Lord, are my eyes: in thee have I put my trust, take not away my soul.
<n>140:9</n> Keep me from the snare, which they have laid for me, * and from the stumbling blocks of them that work iniquity.
<n>140:10</n> The wicked shall fall in his net: * I am alone until I pass.
14.E141:
<n>141:2</n> I cried to the Lord with my voice: * with my voice I made supplication to the Lord.
<n>141:3</n> In his sight I pour out my prayer, * and before him I declare my trouble:
<n>141:4</n> When my spirit failed me, * then thou knewest my paths.
<n>141:4</n> In this way wherein I walked, * they have hidden a snare for me.
<n>141:5</n> I looked on my right hand, and beheld, * and there was no one that would know me.
<n>141:5</n> Flight hath failed me: * and there is no one that hath regard to my soul.
<n>141:6</n> I cried to thee, O Lord: * I said: Thou art my hope, my portion in the land of the living.
<n>141:7</n> Attend to my supplication: * for I am brought very low.
<n>141:7</n> Deliver me from my persecutors; * for they are stronger than I.
<n>141:8</n> Bring my soul out of prison, that I may praise thy name: * the just wait for me, until thou reward me.
14.L143:
<n>143:1</n> Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus meus, qui docet manus meas ad prǽlium, * et dígitos meos ad bellum.
<n>143:2</n> Misericórdia mea, et refúgium meum: * suscéptor meus, et liberátor meus:
<n>143:2</n> Protéctor meus, et in ipso sperávi: * qui subdit pópulum meum sub me.
<n>143:3</n> Dómine, quid est homo, quia innotuísti ei? * aut fílius hóminis, quia réputas eum?
<n>143:4</n> Homo vanitáti símilis factus est: * dies ejus sicut umbra prætéreunt.
<n>143:5</n> Dómine, inclína cælos tuos, et descénde: * tange montes, et fumigábunt.
<n>143:6</n> Fúlgura coruscatiónem, et dissipábis eos: * emítte sagíttas tuas, et conturbábis eos.
<n>143:7</n> Emítte manum tuam de alto, éripe me, et líbera me de aquis multis: * de manu filiórum alienórum.
<n>143:8</n> Quorum os locútum est vanitátem: * et déxtera eórum, déxtera iniquitátis.
<n>143:9</n> Deus, cánticum novum cantábo tibi: * in psaltério decachórdo psallam tibi.
<n>143:10</n> Qui das salútem régibus: * qui redemísti David, servum tuum, de gládio malígno: éripe me.
<n>143:11</n> Et érue me de manu filiórum alienórum, quorum os locútum est vanitátem: * et déxtera eórum, déxtera iniquitátis:
<n>143:12</n> Quorum fílii, sicut novéllæ plantatiónes * in juventúte sua.
<n>143:12</n> Fíliæ eórum compósitæ: * circumornátæ ut similitúdo templi.
<n>143:13</n> Promptuária eórum plena, * eructántia ex hoc in illud.
<n>143:13</n> Oves eórum fœtósæ, abundántes in egréssibus suis: * boves eórum crassæ.
<n>143:14</n> Non est ruína macériæ, neque tránsitus: * neque clamor in platéis eórum.
<n>143:15</n> Beátum dixérunt pópulum, cui hæc sunt: * beátus pópulus, cujus Dóminus Deus ejus.
14.L144:
<n>144:1</n> Exaltábo te, Deus meus, rex: * et benedícam nómini tuo in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
<n>144:2</n> Per síngulos dies benedícam tibi: * et laudábo nomen tuum in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
<n>144:3</n> Magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis: * et magnitúdinis ejus non est finis.
<n>144:4</n> Generátio et generátio laudábit ópera tua: * et poténtiam tuam pronuntiábunt.
<n>144:5</n> Magnificéntiam glóriæ sanctitátis tuæ loquéntur: * et mirabília tua narrábunt.
<n>144:6</n> Et virtútem terribílium tuórum dicent: * et magnitúdinem tuam narrábunt.
<n>144:7</n> Memóriam abundántiæ suavitátis tuæ eructábunt: * et justítia tua exsultábunt.
<n>144:8</n> Miserátor, et miséricors Dóminus: * pátiens, et multum miséricors.
<n>144:9</n> Suávis Dóminus univérsis: * et miseratiónes ejus super ómnia ópera ejus.
<n>144:10</n> Confiteántur tibi, Dómine, ómnia ópera tua: * et sancti tui benedícant tibi.
<n>144:11</n> Glóriam regni tui dicent: * et poténtiam tuam loquéntur:
<n>144:12</n> Ut notam fáciant fíliis hóminum poténtiam tuam: * et glóriam magnificéntiæ regni tui.
<n>144:14</n> Állevat Dóminus omnes qui córruunt: * et érigit omnes elísos.
<n>144:15</n> Óculi ómnium in te sperant, Dómine: * et tu das escam illórum in témpore opportúno.
<n>144:16</n> Áperis tu manum tuam: * et imples omne ánimal benedictióne.
<n>144:17</n> Justus Dóminus in ómnibus viis suis: * et sanctus in ómnibus opéribus suis.
<n>144:18</n> Prope est Dóminus ómnibus invocántibus eum: * ómnibus invocántibus eum in veritáte.
<n>144:19</n> Voluntátem timéntium se fáciet: et deprecatiónem eórum exáudiet: * et salvos fáciet eos.
<n>144:20</n> Custódit Dóminus omnes diligéntes se: * et omnes peccatóres dispérdet.
<n>144:21</n> Laudatiónem Dómini loquétur os meum: * et benedícat omnis caro nómini sancto ejus in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
14.L145:
<n>145:4</n> Exíbit spíritus ejus, et revertétur in terram suam: * in illa die períbunt omnes cogitatiónes eórum.
<n>145:5</n> Beátus, cujus Deus Jacob adjútor ejus, † spes ejus in Dómino, Deo ipsíus: * (6) qui fecit cælum et terram, mare, et ómnia, quæ in eis sunt.
<n>145:9</n> Dóminus custódit ádvenas, † pupíllum et víduam suscípiet: * et vias peccatórum dispérdet.
<n>145:10</n> Regnábit Dóminus in sǽcula, Deus tuus, Sion, * in generatiónem et generatiónem.
14.L146:
<n>146:1</n> Laudáte Dóminum quóniam bonus est psalmus: * Deo nostro sit jucúnda, decóraque laudátio.
<n>146:2</n> Ædíficans Jerúsalem Dóminus: * dispersiónes Israélis congregábit.
<n>146:3</n> Qui sanat contrítos corde: * et álligat contritiónes eórum.
<n>146:4</n> Qui númerat multitúdinem stellárum: * et ómnibus eis nómina vocat.
<n>146:5</n> Magnus Dóminus noster, et magna virtus ejus: * et sapiéntiæ ejus non est númerus.
<n>146:6</n> Suscípiens mansuétos Dóminus: * humílians autem peccatóres usque ad terram.
<n>146:7</n> Præcínite Dómino in confessióne: * psállite Deo nostro in cíthara.
<n>146:9</n> Qui dat juméntis escam ipsórum: * et pullis corvórum invocántibus eum.
<n>146:10</n> Non in fortitúdine equi voluntátem habébit: * nec in tíbiis viri beneplácitum erit ei.
<n>146:11</n> Beneplácitum est Dómino super timéntes eum: * et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia ejus.
14.L147:
<n>147:1</n> Lauda, Jerúsalem, Dóminum: * lauda Deum tuum, Sion.
<n>147:2</n> Quóniam confortávit seras portárum tuárum: * benedíxit fíliis tuis in te.
<n>147:3</n> Qui pósuit fines tuos pacem: * et ádipe fruménti sátiat te.
<n>147:4</n> Qui emíttit elóquium suum terræ: * velóciter currit sermo ejus.
<n>147:5</n> Qui dat nivem sicut lanam: * nébulam sicut cínerem spargit.
<n>147:6</n> Mittit crystállum suam sicut buccéllas: * ante fáciem frígoris ejus quis sustinébit?
<n>147:7</n> Emíttet verbum suum, et liquefáciet ea: * flabit spíritus ejus, et fluent aquæ.
<n>147:8</n> Qui annúntiat verbum suum Jacob: * justítias, et judícia sua Israël.
<n>147:9</n> Non fecit táliter omni natióni: * et judícia sua non manifestávit eis.
14.E143:
<n>143:1</n> Blessed be the Lord my God, who teacheth my hands to fight, * and my fingers to war.
<n>143:2</n> My mercy, and my refuge: * my support, and my deliverer:
<n>143:2</n> My protector, and I have hoped in him: * who subdueth my people under me.
<n>143:3</n> Lord, what is man, that thou art made known to him? * or the son of man, that thou makest account of him?
<n>143:4</n> Man is like to vanity: * his days pass away like a shadow.
<n>143:5</n> Lord, bow down thy heavens and descend: * touch the mountains, and they shall smoke.
<n>143:6</n> Send forth lightning, and thou shalt scatter them: * shoot out thy arrows, and thou shalt trouble them.
<n>143:7</n> Put forth thy hand from on high, take me out, and deliver me from many waters: * from the hand of strange children:
<n>143:8</n> Whose mouth hath spoken vanity: * and their right hand is the right hand of iniquity.
<n>143:9</n> To thee, O God, I will sing a new canticle: * on the psaltery and an instrument of ten strings I will sing praises to thee.
<n>143:10</n> Who givest salvation to kings: * who hast redeemed thy servant David from the malicious sword: Deliver me,
<n>143:11</n> And rescue me out of the hand of strange children; whose mouth hath spoken vanity: * and their right hand is the right hand of iniquity:
<n>143:12</n> Whose sons are as new plants * in their youth:
<n>143:12</n> Their daughters decked out, * adorned round about after the similitude of a temple:
<n>143:13</n> Their storehouses full, * flowing out of this into that.
<n>143:13</n> Their sheep fruitful in young, abounding in their goings forth: * their oxen fat.
<n>143:14</n> There is no breach of wall, nor passage, * nor crying out in their streets.
<n>143:15</n> They have called the people happy, that hath these things: * but happy is that people whose God is the Lord.
14.E144:
<n>144:1</n> I will extol thee, O God my king: * and I will bless thy name for ever; yea, for ever and ever.
<n>144:2</n> Every day will I bless thee: * and I will praise thy name for ever; yea, for ever and ever.
<n>144:3</n> Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised: * and of his greatness there is no end.
<n>144:4</n> Generation and generation shall praise thy works: * and they shall declare thy power.
<n>144:5</n> They shall speak of the magnificence of the glory of thy holiness: * and shall tell thy wondrous works.
<n>144:6</n> And they shall speak of the might of thy terrible acts: * and shall declare thy greatness.
<n>144:7</n> They shall publish the memory of the abundance of thy sweetness: * and shall rejoice in thy justice.
<n>144:8</n> The Lord is gracious and merciful: * patient and plenteous in mercy.
<n>144:9</n> The Lord is sweet to all: * and his tender mercies are over all his works.
<n>144:10</n> Let all thy works, O Lord, praise thee: * and let thy saints bless thee.
<n>144:11</n> They shall speak of the glory of thy kingdom: * and shall tell of thy power:
<n>144:12</n> To make thy might known to the sons of men: * and the glory of the magnificence of thy kingdom.
<n>144:14</n> The Lord lifteth up all that fall: * and setteth up all that are cast down.
<n>144:15</n> The eyes of all hope in thee, O Lord: * and thou givest them meat in due season.
<n>144:16</n> Thou openest thy hand, * and fillest with blessing every living creature.
<n>144:17</n> The Lord is just in all his ways: * and holy in all his works.
<n>144:18</n> The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him: * to all that call upon him in truth.
<n>144:19</n> He will do the will of them that fear him: and he will hear their prayer, * and save them.
<n>144:20</n> The Lord keepeth all them that love him; * but all the wicked he will destroy.
<n>144:21</n> My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord: * and let all flesh bless his holy name for ever; yea, for ever and ever.
14.E145:
<n>145:4</n> His spirit shall go forth, and he shall return into his earth: * in that day all their thoughts shall perish.
<n>145:5</n> Blessed is he who hath the God of Jacob for his helper, † whose hope is in the Lord his God: * (6) who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all things that are in them.
<n>145:9</n> The Lord keepeth the strangers, † he will support the fatherless and the widow: * and the ways of sinners he will destroy.
<n>145:10</n> The Lord shall reign for ever: thy God, O Sion, * unto generation and generation.
14.E146:
<n>146:1</n> Praise ye the Lord, because psalm is good: * to our God be joyful and comely praise.
<n>146:2</n> The Lord buildeth up Jerusalem: * he will gather together the dispersed of Israel.
<n>146:3</n> Who healeth the broken of heart, * and bindeth up their bruises.
<n>146:4</n> Who telleth the number of the stars: * and calleth them all by their names.
<n>146:5</n> Great is our Lord, and great is his power: * and of his wisdom there is no number.
<n>146:6</n> The Lord lifteth up the meek, * and bringeth the wicked down even to the ground.
<n>146:7</n> Sing ye to the Lord with praise: * sing to our God upon the harp.
<n>146:9</n> Who giveth to beasts their food: * and to the young ravens that call upon him.
<n>146:10</n> He shall not delight in the strength of the horse: * nor take pleasure in the legs of a man.
<n>146:11</n> The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him: * and in them that hope in his mercy.
14.E147:
<n>147:1</n> Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem: * praise thy God, O Sion.
<n>147:2</n> Because he hath strengthened the bolts of thy gates * he hath blessed thy children within thee.
<n>147:3</n> Who hath placed peace in thy borders: * and filleth thee with the fat of corn.
<n>147:4</n> Who sendeth forth his speech to the earth: * his word runneth swiftly.
<n>147:5</n> Who giveth snow like wool: * scattereth mists like ashes.
<n>147:6</n> He sendeth his crystal like morsels: * who shall stand before the face of his cold?
<n>147:7</n> He shall send out his word, and shall melt them: * his wind shall blow, and the waters shall run.
<n>147:8</n> Who declareth his word to Jacob: * his justices and his judgments to Israel.
<n>147:9</n> He hath not done in like manner to every nation: * and his judgments he hath not made manifest to them.
